drafts.tip: Treat every decision in the late game as potentially game-deciding, since the margin for error shrinks dramatically once the game reaches the end-game stage.
drafts.rationale: Late-game fights and objective calls resolve so quickly that a single misplay can swing the outcome, unlike earlier phases where mistakes are more recoverable.
drafts.excerpt: You're in the end game now, where any one decision can mean the difference between winning or losing.

drafts.tip: Be willing to sacrifice a piece (an objective, a tower, even a teammate) in order to win the larger fight for the game in the late game.
drafts.rationale: Late-game wins often come from trading a smaller loss for a bigger strategic gain rather than trying to hold onto everything.
drafts.excerpt: In many of the end game scenarios, it is necessary to sacrifice a piece in order to win the game.

drafts.tip: Recognize that a temporary advantage, like a Baron buff, can be more valuable in the late game than a permanent one, like a dragon soul.
drafts.rationale: Temporary power spikes can be leveraged immediately to force objectives or fights, while permanent buffs only matter if you survive long enough to use them.

drafts.tip: Don't tunnel vision on securing one objective, like a dragon soul, if contesting it is hopeless; take mid lane priority instead when that's the smarter play.
drafts.rationale: Chasing a lost objective wastes resources you could instead use to secure map control that's actually winnable.
drafts.excerpt: tunnel vision on the soul, and instead seeked mid priority.

drafts.tip: Recall to reset when you still have enough time before the next objective spawns, rather than forcing a fight.
drafts.rationale: Resetting for items and health before an objective window closes gives you a stronger position than fighting under-prepared.
drafts.excerpt: In this scenario, recalling is the correct option because there's still 23 seconds until the dragon.

drafts.tip: Override your default plan and force a fight immediately if you spot an enemy carry badly out of position.
drafts.rationale: A caught-out enemy carry is a rare, time-sensitive opportunity that outweighs a more conservative default plan like recalling.

drafts.tip: Use the empowered recall from Baron buff to shuttle between objectives faster than the enemy can leverage mid lane priority alone.
drafts.rationale: Faster movement lets you contest or take a second objective before the enemy's priority advantage can be converted.
drafts.excerpt: And therefore, we have the empowered recalls, which allows us to move from the dragon to our base much faster.

drafts.tip: When a fight or scenario goes wrong in the late game, first ask yourself how you can survive before anything else.
drafts.rationale: Securing survival preserves your options; a dead champion has no further influence on the game.
drafts.excerpt: I have two questions that you need to be asking yourself. Ask yourself Varus ADC dies in the mid lane. You need to ask yourself first, how can we survive?

drafts.tip: Once survival is secured, shift your focus to the second question: how can we win?
drafts.rationale: Separating the two questions keeps you from either recklessly forcing a win attempt too early or passively surviving without ever pivoting to close the game.
drafts.excerpt: Okay, that's the first one. And the second, how can we win?

drafts.tip: When you can't fight the enemy directly because they have a big advantage, buy time with baiting and distraction rather than committing to a fight.
drafts.rationale: Staying alive and stalling preserves options for a comeback that an unwinnable fight would remove.
drafts.excerpt: So, I'm always moving up a little bit, trying to bait the opponents in, but not actively wanting to fight with them.

drafts.tip: Don't let the surrender vote distract you; keep focusing on the actual situation on the map instead.
drafts.rationale: The surrender prompt is a mental distraction that can pull attention away from actionable information like enemy cooldowns and positioning.
drafts.excerpt: The situation looks very dire, and in the bottom right corner, the surrender vote appears. But I don't look at that. I focus on the situation.

drafts.tip: Recognize when a fight is unwinnable and disengage immediately rather than continuing to trade.
drafts.rationale: Continuing to fight a losing engagement only compounds the loss, while a clean disengage preserves the chance to stall or come back.
drafts.excerpt: win this fight, so I immediately disengage.

drafts.tip: Don't give up on the game even when it looks over; keep observing what's happening and stay ready to play for a comeback.
drafts.rationale: Games are frequently won after they appear lost when players stay engaged and keep looking for openings instead of checking out mentally.
drafts.excerpt: However, my Lucian and Vayne still keep playing the game, and I keep observing what is happening.

drafts.tip: When pushing to close out the game on the Nexus, prioritize not dying to the defenders over dealing extra damage.
drafts.rationale: Dying while trying to end the game can swing a nearly-won fight back to the enemy, while staying alive keeps the pressure on.
drafts.excerpt: not dying to the enemies that try to defend the Nexus towers.

drafts.tip: As an engage support like Pyke, delay committing your all-in ultimate until it can also catch a secondary target, even if that means letting an ally act as bait first.
drafts.rationale: Landing the ultimate on two targets instead of one converts a single pick into a much bigger swing for the fight.

drafts.tip: Identify the enemy's most dangerous threat and focus your peel on keeping them away from your carries, rather than spreading your attention evenly.
drafts.rationale: Neutralizing the single biggest damage threat protects your win condition more effectively than splitting focus across all enemies.
drafts.excerpt: Next up, we're going to focus on getting the Singed away from our carries. The Singed is the most dangerous part of the enemy team.

drafts.tip: Refuse to surrender and keep fighting even when your team wants to give up; that persistence alone is sometimes enough to win.
drafts.rationale: A team that keeps contesting fights and objectives retains a chance to win, while surrendering guarantees the loss.

drafts.tip: In low elo, pick carry supports like Zyra or Senna so you can win games on your own rather than depending on your ADC.
drafts.rationale: A traditional support's lead is shared with the ADC, so solo agency converts to wins more reliably.
drafts.excerpt: start of the climb was to pick carry supports, mainly Zyra and Senna, because in low elo it's better to be able to carry yourself than to rely on your team.

drafts.tip: Winning lane on a non-carry support is unreliable, since it depends on your ADC actually being able to utilize the lead you build.
drafts.rationale: A support-side lane win only converts to a game win if the ADC can execute on it, which is not guaranteed at low elo.
drafts.excerpt: worse than a coin flip if your ADC can actually utilize their lead and it's just better to have solo agency as a support so you can actually carry yourself.

drafts.tip: Understand that unless you're playing a carry support, any lead you build is shared with your ADC and can't be independently converted into a win the way other roles can.
drafts.rationale: Traditional supports lack the individual power to close games alone, capping how much a solo lead can accomplish.
drafts.excerpt: a carry support, the lead you build is largely shared with your ADC carry and traditional supports have a more limited ability to take over games on their own.

drafts.tip: Don't assume a bot lane win guarantees a carried game; below around diamond, ADCs often can't pilot their champion well enough to convert a lead you've given them.
drafts.rationale: ADC mechanical and macro consistency is inconsistent at lower ranks, so the support's lane win can go to waste.
drafts.excerpt: start of the climb, I would always be able to win lane but my ADCs would just not be able to pilot their champion well enough to carry.

drafts.tip: In lower elo, ADCs usually aren't able to carry a lead until around diamond plus.
drafts.rationale: This sets a practical rank threshold for when relying on your ADC to close games becomes reasonable.
drafts.excerpt: usually aren't able to carry until around diamond plus.

drafts.tip: In lower elo, don't let a good counter-pick lane matchup tempt you into a traditional support; comp matters less than just playing a carry support.
drafts.rationale: At low elo the ability to solo-carry outweighs the marginal edge of a favorable draft matchup.
drafts.excerpt: myself into playing a traditional support when I had a good counter pick in lane but in lower elo, comp does not matter as much as playing as a carry support.

drafts.tip: You can still climb on regular (non-carry) supports in low elo, but expect a lot more games where you lose despite playing well.
drafts.rationale: Traditional supports depend on teammates who aren't consistently able to convert leads at low elo, so good individual play doesn't guarantee a win.
drafts.excerpt: in lower elo but there are going to be a lot more games where you are going to lose despite playing very well.

drafts.tip: Test traditional supports occasionally as you climb to find the rank where you can transition back to playing them as your main champions.
drafts.rationale: Gradually testing lets you find the point where teammate reliability makes non-carry supports viable again, instead of guessing.
drafts.excerpt: ranks I could start playing traditional supports. I basically did this until around D2 plus where I started playing my main champs which are mostly enchanters.

drafts.tip: Diamond is roughly the rank where teammates start to become reliably capable, regardless of server.
drafts.rationale: This gives a concrete benchmark for when to trust teammates to follow up on plays and execute leads.
drafts.excerpt: diamond is a rank where teammates universally start to feel more human and reliable.

drafts.tip: Carry supports' advantage of brute-forcing a lead alone gradually diminishes as you climb.
drafts.rationale: Higher-elo teammates are more capable, reducing the relative value of a support who can win games single-handedly.
drafts.excerpt: they can brute force leads on their own but their impact gradually falls off as you climb.

drafts.tip: Engage, enchanter, and hook supports get stronger the higher you climb, since they depend on team coordination and follow-up that only shows up reliably at higher elo.
drafts.rationale: These champion types rely on teammates capitalizing on their setup, which becomes more consistent as skill increases.

drafts.rationale: Unlike last season, the gold-per-10 gap between tiers means delaying the finished item now costs significantly more value over time.

drafts.tip: Build World Atlas stacks quickly by constantly keeping a stack charging and spending most stacks on hitting enemy champions.
drafts.rationale: Champion damage yields more gold than minion last hits, so prioritizing it accelerates the item's completion.

drafts.rationale: Homeguard's bonus movement speed is spent while traveling, so routing through a lane gets the most value out of it before it expires.

drafts.rationale: Flanking through the jungle avoids revealing your approach to the lane you're ganking, increasing the chance of a successful play.
drafts.excerpt: To optimize roaming, you most likely want to dip into the jungle when you're further out and want to flank from the side.

drafts.tip: If you're playing a tanky support, prioritize getting brush control as soon as possible so you can engage safely from stealth.
drafts.rationale: Brush hides you from enemy vision, letting a tanky support initiate on the carry without being punished first.

drafts.tip: If you're playing an enchanter, focus on damaging and harassing the enemy ADC while shielding your own team's damage taken.
drafts.rationale: Enchanters win lane through consistent poke and mitigation rather than all-in engage.

drafts.tip: If you're playing a bully support, keep poking the enemy ADC until they run low on health.
drafts.rationale: Bully supports win lane by attrition rather than a single all-in.
drafts.excerpt: And if you're a bully support, just keep throwing things at the enemy AD carry until they run low on health.

drafts.tip: Read your ADC's power spike and adjust your playstyle: expect to play aggressively with an early-game carry like Draven or Lucian, and expect a scaling carry like Jinx or Veigar to prefer sitting back and farming.
drafts.rationale: Matching your lane approach to your carry's win condition avoids fighting against your own ADC's strengths.

drafts.tip: As support, you're not really responsible for controlling the wave, but you are very responsible for taking good trades.
drafts.rationale: This reflects the division of labor in bot lane: the carry manages farm while the support's value comes from trade decisions.

drafts.tip: Take trades where you either deal more damage than you take, or put your opponent in a difficult situation to stay in the lane.
drafts.rationale: Treating your health bar as a resource means only committing to exchanges that net a clear advantage.
drafts.excerpt: essentially want to take fights where you either deal more damage than you take, or you put your opponent in a difficult situation to stay in the lane.

drafts.tip: Look to fight when you hit level two, three, or six before your opponent, since you'll temporarily have an extra ability advantage.
drafts.rationale: A one-ability lead is a significant power spike that makes trades much more favorable during that window.
drafts.excerpt: to pick fights. You'll have one more ability than your opponent, which is very strong.

drafts.tip: Also look for trades when the enemy has used abilities on minions, is low on mana, or when you have an item advantage after backing.
drafts.rationale: These moments represent a temporary power or resource deficit for the opponent that makes them vulnerable.
drafts.excerpt: Also, if they've ever used abilities on minions, or running low on mana, or if you've backed and have the item advantage, look for trade.

drafts.tip: If your carry needs to back and you don't, use the opportunity to roam mid.
drafts.rationale: A back from your carry frees you from lane responsibilities, making it an efficient window to apply pressure elsewhere.
drafts.excerpt: You also want to look for opportunities where you're able to roam. If your carry needs to back and you don't, roam mid.

drafts.tip: After backing, consider heading to mid lane first, then rotating to bot lane about 10 seconds later.
drafts.rationale: This sequencing lets you apply pressure mid before returning to your primary lane, extracting extra value from the back.

drafts.tip: Ganking the enemy mid laner as support is very strong, since your lockdown and damage are often enough alone to secure the kill.
drafts.rationale: Supports bring crowd control and burst that most mid laners aren't itemized against early, making these ganks efficient.
drafts.excerpt: Ganking the enemy mid laner as support is very strong. With the lockdown and damage you provide often being enough to get the kill.

drafts.tip: When dragon spawns, make sure you're there helping contest it.
drafts.rationale: Objective fights typically require full team presence, and missing them cedes an uncontested advantage to the enemy.
